title: The Church of the East
hook: Christians who traveled the Silk Road to China and India in the first millennium

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was Oriental Orthodox: Copts, Ethiopians, Armenians, Syriacs and the Malankara church. Your line was very old, still singing.

In the 1620s, workers digging near Xi'an, in China, pulled a huge stone slab out of the ground. Taller than a man, with a cross carved at the top, rising out of a lotus flower. Below it, nearly two thousand Chinese characters, and a border of writing in Syriac. The stone had been set up in 781. It told how a monk named Alopen reached the Tang emperor's capital in 635, carrying scriptures, and how the emperor welcomed him, had the books translated, and let him build a monastery. Christians in China, in the 600s.
screen: `A STONE FROM THE YEAR 781.` → `A CROSS RISING FROM A LOTUS.` → `CHRISTIANS IN CHINA, 635.`

segments.voice: The Church of the East grew up in Persia, beyond the Roman Empire's eastern border, among Christians who prayed in Syriac, a cousin of Jesus's own Aramaic. Its leader, the catholicos, sat in Seleucia-Ctesiphon, near modern Baghdad. Outside Rome, it went its own way on the councils. Westerners long called it Nestorian, after a bishop condemned in 431, a label the church didn't choose and many today find misleading. Along the Silk Road, with its caravans, oases and monasteries, merchants and monks from this church carried the gospel across Central Asia to China, and down to India, where the Saint Thomas Christians trace their faith to the apostle Thomas himself. In China they called their faith the luminous teaching. At its height, around 1300, this one church stretched from the Mediterranean to the Pacific, with more territory than any church in Europe. A monk from near Beijing, Rabban Sauma, traveled west and met the king of France in 1287, and the pope in 1288. Then came centuries of hardship: plagues, conquests, the collapse of the Mongol empire, massacres. The church shrank almost to nothing in China and Central Asia. Its heirs today, the Assyrian Church of the East, the Ancient Church of the East, and churches in communion with Rome such as the Chaldeans, are small, many of them refugees from Iraq and Syria. In Acts, Jesus told his friends they would be his witnesses "unto the uttermost part of the earth." Most maps of Christian history draw that line going west. This church went east too, early and far.
screen: `A CHURCH BEYOND ROME, IN PERSIA.` · `A LABEL IT DIDN'T CHOOSE.` · `ALONG THE SILK ROAD TO CHINA.` · `SMALL NOW, MANY OF THEM REFUGEES.` · then, large: `UNTO THE UTTERMOST PART OF THE EARTH.`

segments.voice: On a map of Asia, trace a finger from Baghdad east, across Iran and the mountains of Central Asia, to Xi'an; then back, and down to Kerala, on India's southwest coast. Thousands of miles, walked by monks and merchants more than a thousand years ago. If you pray, pray for the Christians who still live along that road, and those who had to leave it; if not, let the size of the map sink in.
Luminous teaching. What the Church of the East's faith was called in Tang China, carried there along the Silk Road.
Your line: the road went east. By 635 it had reached the Tang capital. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: The Assyrian Church of the East and its sister churches still pray in Syriac, keep an ancient liturgy called the Liturgy of Addai and Mari, and honor the cross without a figure on it.

notes: Xi'an Stele: discovered c. 1623–1625; erected 781; describes Alopen's arrival in 635 under Emperor Taizong. Character count about 1,800–2,000. Confirm.
The cross-on-lotus image at the top of the stele: confirm description.
'At its height... more territory than any church in Europe': a common claim among historians (e.g. about the 13th–14th centuries). Confirm phrasing.
Rabban Sauma met Pope Nicholas IV and Philip IV of France (1287–1288); confirm he met the pope in 1288 (Nicholas was elected Feb 1288) — script says 'in 1287' for the journey; may need '1287–88'.
Nestorius condemned at Ephesus (431). The Church of the East's relation to Nestorius is debated; the label is described as outside and misleading.
Heirs: Assyrian Church of the East, Ancient Church of the East, Chaldean Catholic Church; Saint Thomas Christians in India have historic ties (e.g. Syro-Malabar). Confirm.
Chinese 景教 (jǐngjiào) pronunciation guide is approximate.
